## Trial `zram-swap-ubuntu24__boG4b2a`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully configured a 512MB zstd-compressed zram swap on node1 via systemd-zram-generator, resolved a genuine kernel-module gap (installing linux-modules-extra) along the way, and set swap-priority=100 with no disk-backed swap present. All three material outcomes (size/compression, boot activation, priority preference) are directly and consistently evidenced, including a real reboot cycle with matching boot-identity change confirmed by the independent fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-reboot re-verification of the swap state. The only notable inefficiency is one unnecessary package reinstall during troubleshooting that did not contribute to the fix, a minor and low-risk hygiene issue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 16/3 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured on node1
  - **Why:** systemd-zram-generator configured with zram0 at 512MB and zstd compression. swapon --show and /proc/swaps confirm a 524284KB (512MiB) /dev/zram0 swap device is active, and /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows [zstd] selected. Verified both immediately after setup and again after a full reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ab2a6173699d4eaf`, `cmd-230d1dfbb21541d0`, `cmd-473e021d39c943b6`, `cmd-04b020b25d0045a1`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Swap is active at boot without manual intervention
  - **Why:** dev-zram0.swap is auto-generated under /run/systemd/generator/swap.target.wants and wired to swap.target via the persisted /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf, so it is regenerated every boot with no manual enable step. This was directly validated by a real reboot: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the post-restart boot_id differed (confirmed independently by the fixed lifecycle before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots), and the zram swap was found active at 512M/zstd/priority 100 immediately after, with systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service exited successfully with no manual commands run in between.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-473e021d39c943b6`, `cmd-edae5d775c7d4daa`, `cmd-49b4177ebea24236`, `cmd-e851e0a6e4144df0`, `cmd-04b020b25d0045a1`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
  - **Why:** swap-priority=100 is set in the zram-generator config and reflected in swapon --show output (PRIO 100). No disk-backed swap exists on the node either before or after configuration (/proc/swaps and swapon --show show only /dev/zram0 at every check), so zram is the exclusive and highest-priority swap source, satisfying the preference requirement.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c7f0fec61d64431d`, `cmd-230d1dfbb21541d0`, `cmd-04b020b25d0045a1`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Most executor commands were read-only diagnostics or directly contributed to the fix (installing systemd-zram-generator, writing the config, discovering and installing linux-modules-extra to supply the missing zram.ko, loading/testing the module, restarting the setup service). One unnecessary mutation occurred: cmd-42958399701548cd reinstalled the already-installed linux-modules-6.8.0-71-generic package (same version) as a troubleshooting attempt to find zram.ko; this did not resolve the issue (the module was still missing immediately afterward per cmd-e4141637a3ba4cc7) and the real fix was installing the separate linux-modules-extra package. The reinstall triggered an initramfs/grub regeneration, a low-risk but unnecessary side effect that was not reverted, though it left no harmful residue (same-version reinstall, no config drift). No abandoned files, failed services, weakened security, or unsafe exposure were observed; failed-services and package-health checks are clean before and after.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-42958399701548cd`, `cmd-e4141637a3ba4cc7`, `cmd-a7c998425f1a4a48`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`
